label: z drops for a1/S1 (and after a1->S2 at D1), rises for a2/S2; belief S1 lowers
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 16 sits near 1 (mean 0.984) and dips. Beyond timing it follows the a1/S1 vs a2/S2 axis using observed cues only: at D2 it is lowest after choosing a1 and reaching S1 (common) and highest after choosing a2; at D1 it dips sharply when the previous trial was a1 -> S2 (rare), regardless of reward, and is slightly raised after a2 -> S1; at GO it is a bit lower after a previous a1 than a2. On top of this, the ideal-observer belief that S1 is good lowers z graded in every phase (strongest at D2). All effects grow later in the episode (scaled by 1+ep_trial/50, which helped dev 0.632 -> 0.649). Reward itself and future variables add little (this-trial reward reference 0.01). Test R^2 beyond timing 0.65 (dev 0.66), vs all ceiling 0.77 and all-observed 0.73, so about 85% of the ceiling; replacing the model policy (policy-decile reference 0.48) with belief + trial history loses essentially nothing.

issues: The late-episode scaling has the wrong shape. The worst-fit dev windows from misses all sit at trials 92-99, where actual z drops far below the prediction (e.g. D2 0.83-0.87 actual vs 0.925 predicted; D1 0.85-0.90 vs 0.94-0.97). The effects grow faster than linearly near episode end. With the same terms, scaling by (1+ep_trial/50+(ep_trial>=90)) gives test 0.699 instead of 0.655, and adding steps at 85 and 95 gives 0.700. So '(1+ep_trial/50)' understates how concentrated the growth is in the final ~10 trials.

Previous-trial reward is missing at D2. The profile shows D2 residuals after a1 S2 r = +0.006 vs a1 S2 u = -0.024, and after a2 S2 r = +0.014 vs a2 S2 u = +0.004. Misses on the original terms lists D2 after a1 S2 r (+0.009) as most under-predicted and D2 after a1 S2 u (-0.010) as most over-predicted. Replacing the weak D1 belief term with (phase==D2)*(prev_reward==1)*S raises test R^2 from 0.655 to 0.672. The claim that 'reward adds little' only holds for this trial's (future) reward. The previous reward visibly raises z at D2.

The claim that belief lowers z 'most strongly at D2' holds in the raw belief-decile residuals but not in the fitted model. The D2 belief weight (-0.0013) is smaller than the GO weight (-0.0019), because the a1/S1 and a2 terms absorb the D2 effect. Each belief term adds only about 0.01-0.02 test R^2 when dropped one at a time (drop D1: 0.644, GO: 0.638, D2: 0.633).

These claims check out: the a2-at-D2 term is the largest single contributor (dropping it gives 0.512); the D1 dip after a1->S2 does not depend on reward (residual -0.026 rewarded vs -0.021 unrewarded); there is a small D1 rise after a2->S1 and a GO effect of the previous choice (dropping it gives 0.549). No future variables are used, and the reported test R^2 of 0.6546 reproduces exactly.
The improved terms below still leave about 0.03 to the all-observed ceiling (0.73). After the fix, the remaining misses are small (<=0.006 per cell).
skeptic.revised_label: z dips for a1/S1, rises for a2/S2 (D2), dips at D1 after rare a1->S2; raised at D2 after prior reward; belief S1 lowers; effects surge in last ~10 trials
